material_risks.detail: Inherited source phase is not an observation of reconstruction phase. Static z with changing source psi does not produce an affine transported q; transporting a constant reconstruction can change it. Endogenous B/D cancellation is preserved only when the resulting C coefficient obeys the transported affine law, not for arbitrary phase mismatch.

Pure algebra for a fixed-coordinate quadratic coefficient a+b*t+q*t^2 gives endpoint bias -q*(n-1)*(n-2)/6, hence -35q atn16. This is independent of data/quality and shows degree1 cannot preserve curvature or accelerating phase.

Atn16 negative weights sum -5/17, L1 weight sum27/17, current-frame step gain31/136, and a persistent step can reach22/17 at11 newest post-step samples (29.4% overshoot). Source-phase/DC cuts do not guarantee every native reconstruction coefficient change is detected. Bounds are pure weight sums, not scored scene/operator behavior.

31/136 is IID equal-variance coefficient-noise algebra only. Actual variance is w^T*Sigma*w; endogenous B/D, RGB/time correlation, phase errors and persistent common bias invalidate confidence/noise-gain claims. Unit-sum weights preserve constant bias rather than identify clean radiance.

Dense current residual is deliberately retained. Frozen DC replacement and per-pixel RGB fallback can alter final decomposition and gain/phase. Low temporal variance alone can mask true current nonlinear detail or stale native history; all frozen quality gates remain necessary.
